basis: Personal complete live-browser reading of the three assigned introductions, sections, tables, code, current CPU output widgets, and exercises; notes below are my own interpretation, not an execution claim.

sections.5.1: Fixed-example memorization diagnoses clear/forward/backward/step ordering. The all -100 exercise intentionally rejects empty supervision; the 40-step width-8 diagnostic is distinct from the 600-step width-64 GPU record.
sections.5.2: Five valid targets, rather than two equally weighted records or eight padded cells, determine the mean. Adding the sixth uniform target increases the sum but leaves the log(5) mean unchanged.
sections.5.3: A stored velocity keeps the third update moving negative despite the new negative gradient. This history is explicitly distinguished from accumulating .grad.
sections.5.4: Adam’s m and squared-gradient v are declared locally; first-step bias correction cancels the scale difference of gradients 1 and 100. Later history may prevent equal updates.
sections.5.5: With task gradient zero, decoupled decay changes 2 to 1.96. None skips the parameter in this implementation, so the two exercises test separate participation and decay controls.
sections.5.6: Zero-based warmup indices, peak and 10% floor are stated alongside clipping warmup to the available plan. Changing total planned steps changes the later schedule, which matters for resume.
sections.5.7: The one-step save/reload first matches predictions and then matches the next update only when optimizer history is restored. Token meanings, RNG, sampling, and the planned schedule remain additional state obligations.
sections.5.8: Teacher-forced token success and autonomous whole-answer success use different previous tokens. The left/right continuation has no supplied side truth; later shape-question errors do, so the evaluation goal changes explicitly.
sections.5.9: Parameter payload, forward timing, training interval, and whole-experiment time have distinct denominators and hardware. Increasing sequence length changes work without changing parameters.
sections.5.10: Validation participates in selection, test remains withheld, and the chosen maximum is not an independent final score. Upstream train filenames do not define this project’s internal split purpose.
sections.5.11: Whitespace normalization is a data-comparison rule rather than LayerNorm. The fingerprint counts unique normalized content but does not determine meaning or remove near duplicates.
sections.5.12: Jaccard overlap groups similar versions without erasing opposite labels. The actual stories/poems experiment admits that near-family separation is incomplete.
sections.5.13: The four-cell plan is not measured quality; the separate 150-step experiment changes width and unique records while disclosing unequal valid-target exposure. The exercise computes the required 200 updates from a fixed token budget.
sections.5.14: Every learning-rate candidate starts from the same w. The large step reaches 9 and worsens square loss; the altered-start exercise keeps the same relative error factors, avoiding an unsupported optimum claim.
sections.5.15: Seeds control random routes, not quality rankings. Initialization spread is not performance, and paired seeds do not guarantee identical data draws if architectures consume RNG differently.
sections.5.16: 90 short records and 10 long records produce 90 versus 200 supervised positions. Weighting loss is distinguished from changing those counts, and the replay example carries this budget distinction forward.
sections.5.17: eval changes module behavior, no_grad changes this computation’s recording, and freezing changes parameter participation. A frozen Linear can still transmit gradients to a trainable input.
sections.6.1: Code points, UTF-8 bytes, and model tokens differ. The replacement symbol in a truncated poem is attributed to generated incomplete bytes, not to an already-broken prompt.
sections.6.2: Pair counts stay within documents and merges are nonoverlapping. Adding acacacac changes the most frequent pair without asserting that every merged token is a linguistic word.
sections.6.3: ByteLevel’s full alphabet permits unseen Unicode round trips; its visible byte symbols are not corrupt text. This tokenizer training learns encoding rules rather than model weights.
sections.6.4: Vocabulary enlarges separate input/output tables while potentially shortening sequences. The current 264/512 comparison reports both sequence counts and different parameter counts.
sections.6.5: NLL sums conditional prediction events; it does not assume independent text tokens. Common original bytes and a shared EOS convention resolve the per-token ranking reversal while leaving compute budgets unequal.
sections.6.6: Content bytes shifted by 8 cannot collide with eight structural IDs. Literal assistant text remains content, and actual role insertion comes from fields; the BPE claim includes its normal-content encoding policy.
sections.6.7: A partial Unicode byte tail produces a replacement character when decoded alone. Preserving raw bytes and decoding enough material is distinct from pretending every BPE token is a whole character.
sections.6.8: C input/target pairs need C+1 raw IDs and exactly one shift. File grouping precedes windows, and the failed tail-window exercise changes the window contract rather than tokenizer rules.
sections.6.9: Whitespace hello versus hel/lo isolates the lost merge opportunity. The different preprocessing policy is explicitly scoped away from the earlier lossless ByteLevel example.
sections.7.1: Structured roles serialize BOS/user/question/EOS/assistant/answer/EOS. The effective targets are answer bytes plus EOS; changing only the arithmetic question intentionally leaves an incorrect demonstration to reveal the distinction.
sections.7.2: The nine-token inference prompt stops at assistant and excludes the unknown answer. Removing assistant changes the interface and deliberately fails the boundary check.
sections.7.3: Shifted labels choose supervision, while valid IDs remain in X. A Chinese answer contributes three bytes plus EOS; the exercises count six bytes plus EOS or two ASCII bytes plus EOS.
sections.7.4: Assistant at position 4 predicts A, and A at position 5 predicts EOS. Extending Q moves the physical index without moving the role-ID meaning; the model must not shift again.
sections.7.5: The ignored BOS output has zero direct logit gradient, but question Q’s embedding row receives later-answer influence. Retaining a nonleaf gradient and querying by token ID answer different questions.
sections.7.6: Appending ignored label cells preserves the same two scored predictions and denominator. The example explicitly does not claim that a real padded model forward is unchanged.
sections.7.7: PAD-key exclusion and preserved semantic position IDs are both required for left-padding equivalence. Empty key rows are handled numerically; the exercises remove each condition separately.
sections.7.8: Maximum physical valid index works for both padding sides; sum(valid)-1 fails for left padding. Empty inputs need rejection, and this does not turn the simple generator into a complete padded batch generator.
sections.7.9: Learning EOS, generation’s EOS test, and the new-token cap are separate steps. Cire plus EOS is a stopped but incorrect answer, and historic user EOS does not stop a new answer.
sections.7.10: A truncated input can have no valid answer. Length 19 preserves one byte target at the assistant position, whereas 22 preserves all three bytes and EOS; the small UltraChat fragments are scoped to their incomplete meanings.
sections.7.11: The displayed CPU example reaches backward without step. Genuine SFT loads the matching base and tokenizer; the actual text→chat branch uses the same 45-question material and has 250 extra updates.
sections.7.12: Holding out red-square retains individual color/shape coverage but tests a new combination. The actual 9/1/2 families and 45/5/10 questions use shared valid-target denominators and separate answer/EOS checks.
sections.7.13: JSON format can pass while arithmetic fails. The baseline is deliberately the direct-SFT checkpoint with 5/10 success, rather than quietly substituting the better text→SFT branch.
sections.7.14: Cross entropy follows the supplied wrong label; the four-class toy IDs are declared separately from byte IDs. The paired noisy/clean continuation uses the same questions and target exposure, and lower loss can coexist with fewer exact answers.
sections.7.15: The four before/after task cells can show old-task degradation without new-task held-out improvement. Swapped addends stay in one family; the actual experiment does not call reduced new-task loss a successful arithmetic skill.
sections.7.16: Replay recomputes old-data gradients with current weights. The actual 500-step recipe improves old-task retention but has nearly double the target exposure and still fails new held-out addition.
sections.7.17: Natural text supplies its own next-item targets while checked chat requires task-specific answers. Reusable bases and optional branching are motivated without treating toy data costs or 250 extra steps as causal proof.
sections.7.18: Demonstrations, preferences, and scored answers supply different signals. SFT, DPO, RLHF, PPO, and program-verifiable feedback retain distinct meanings; the changed-task exercise requires rebuilding judgments rather than merely swapping chosen/rejected.

boundaries.04_to_05: 4.8 distinguishes extra architectural capacity/cost from measured learning; 5.1 then supplies the actual parameter-update loop after 4.7’s gradient-only interface.
boundaries.05_to_06: 5.17 completes the computational controls; chapter 6 introduces a separate data interface whose token units alter the previously established target and resource counts.
boundaries.06_to_07: 6.6 supplies control/content IDs, 6.7 supplies byte counting, and 6.8 supplies shift/window contracts before 7.1 serializes a dialogue. Ending 6.9 keeps I/O chunks distinct from those semantic roles.
boundaries.07_to_08: 7.13 separates content and format, while 7.17–7.18 distinguish teaching goals and methods. Chapter 8’s introduction and 8.1 keep correct arithmetic separate from helpful expression instead of redefining dialogue success.
